transformations.edit: Replaced the seed string recorder with an executable Verus function for the Rust 1.96 target body.
Adapted the inherent `[T]` receiver to an explicit `slice: &[T]` parameter, removed `const`, and named the return value for Verus; no target-body path was externalized or assumed.

Lowered the unsupported Rust slice pattern `if let [first, tail @ ..] = self` to the mechanically equivalent nonempty branch `slice.len() != 0`, `slice.split_at(1)`, and `&head[0]`; a direct slice-pattern diagnostic shows Verus rejects slice patterns, so the desugaring preserves the same first-element/tail data flow for verification.

Added proof-only `lemma_split_at` and equality assertions connecting the desugared head/tail views to the generated `slice@[0]` and `slice@.subrange(1, len)` contract; these annotations do not change executable control flow or data flow.
